# Shock mount stud replacement

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Grind down existing factory studs on both rear shock absorbers to drill out areas for new bolts. [t547]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the rear shock absorber from both sides.
2. [Partial] Grind down the existing factory stud on the frame where it connects to the bracket.

_Procedure reported by [t547]._

## Tools

- [Partial] Angle grinder [t547]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Drill out the ground area and install a new bolt or stud in the same location. [t547]
- Consider using Grade 8 bolts for suspension as they are stronger than standard Grade 5. [t547]
